applicant_utility.summary: This is a country-restricted award: if your passport is not one of the ten named countries, nothing else on this page applies to you. If it is, note that the round is annual and closed in May, so you have a long window between rounds to line up the documents that actually decide the outcome - the CSCA score for bachelor's applicants, HSK 5 at 210 or above for Chinese-taught programmes, and an IELTS 6.0/TOEFL 80/Duolingo 105 or English-medium instruction letter for English-taught programmes. The application is genuinely two-stage: you must first be interviewed and nominated by Nankai before you are allowed to touch the CSC portal, so a late or incomplete Nankai submission ends the process before the CSC stage even opens. Master's applicants should treat the 800-word personal statement, with a China study and research plan, as the main piece they control.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Nationals of the ten named countries who want a business, finance or international-affairs degree in Tianjin and already hold (or can quickly get) the required CSCA or HSK 5 score.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your nationality is on the ten-country list before investing any effort, since no other route into this scholarship exists
Book the CSCA test early if applying at bachelor's level; the score report is a required upload, not an optional extra
Get your passport valid past 1 September 2027 of the intake year, and if you are already in mainland China keep your visa or residence permit current
For English-taught master's programmes, either sit IELTS/TOEFL/Duolingo or request the official English-medium instruction letter from your previous university well in advance
Have every non-Chinese/English certificate notarised and translated before you start uploading, since translation is a prerequisite, not a follow-up
Complete the Foreigner Physical Examination Form at a hospital that covers every listed item, and date it inside the validity window the call specifies (after October 2025 for this round)
common_rejection_risks: Applying through the CSC portal directly and never completing the Nankai platform application, which is the only way to be nominated
Uploading phone photographs or photocopies, which the call explicitly refuses; only colour scanner PDFs are accepted
Leaving the interview email unread because it lands in the system inbox rather than your personal mailbox
Submitting a personal statement under the 800-word floor for master's applicants, or one that omits the China study and research plan
Holding another scholarship simultaneously, which is a stated bar
Missing the age ceilings of 25 (bachelor's) and 35 (master's)
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Airfare to and from China, visa and residence-permit fees, and any accommodation outside the free on-campus allocation are not funded; the award does not publish an on-campus accommodation cap, so confirm with the School of International Education whether a room is guaranteed for your campus.
document_audit: Passport expiry is tested against a fixed future date (1 September 2027), so renew it before you apply rather than after
Every non-English/Chinese certificate, including transcripts, needs a notarised translation attached to the same upload
Graduating students use a pre-graduation certificate, so plan to submit your final degree certificate later at registration
The two master's referees must be associate or full professors; a line manager or lecturer letter is not accepted
The Malaysian independent Chinese secondary school exemption for HSK still needs your graduation certificate attached as proof
alerts: The published deadline is for the closed 2026 round; the next call will appear on the same Nankai pages, so watch the site rather than relying on this date
The programme list is explicitly subject to China Scholarship Council approval, so a programme you see published can disappear
Nomination is capped by quota, so Nankai reviews and interviews before the CSC ever sees the file, which makes timing as important as eligibility
Be careful not to double-apply through other channels: holding any other scholarship disqualifies you here
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply on Nankai's own platform first, wait for the system-email interview invitation, and only after nomination and pre-admission complete the CSC Type B application naming agency 10055.

official.application_route: Single online submission through the UCAS Online Admission System for International Students at is.ucas.ac.cn, selecting the scholarship within the admission application; no separate portal.

applicant_utility.summary: UCAS runs a single online route, so there is no embassy or agency nomination step to chase: you apply once through is.ucas.ac.cn and tick the scholarship inside that same application, which means your scholarship case is decided on your admission file. Because the full tier adds a supervisor/faculty research assistantship on top of the RMB 2,000-2,500 base stipend, your realistic monthly income depends on the host institute you choose, so research which CAS institute you are applying to before you commit. Two hard bars catch applicants out: you are excluded if you are already studying for a master's or doctoral degree anywhere in China, and you may not approach two supervisors at once, so contact one potential supervisor deliberately and early.
applicant_utility.best_fit: International Master's and PhD applicants who want a single-portal application to research institutes across the Chinese Academy of Sciences system and need tuition plus a guaranteed stipend.
application_readiness_checklist: Identify the target UCAS college or CAS institute first and use the supervisor directory to secure an informal acceptance, since the Supervisor's Acceptance Form strengthens the file even though it is optional
Sit IELTS or TOEFL (or assemble another accepted proof of English) unless your mother tongue is English; the scholarship call gives no score but the admission call asks for a valid certificate
For Chinese-instructed programmes, reach HSK 5 with at least 180, which is the admission call's threshold rather than the scholarship's
Ask your two referees to write on institutional letterhead with signature and date, and make sure neither is your prospective UCAS supervisor
Combine every non-English/Chinese original and its translation into a single PDF before uploading, as the call requires one combined file
Check your passport has at least one year of validity remaining and that your nationality cancellation documents are in order if you formerly held Chinese citizenship
common_rejection_risks: Already being enrolled on a master's or doctoral programme in China, which disqualifies the corresponding programme and is reported to your current institution
Creating two accounts or filing duplicate applications, both of which are checked and lead to disqualification
Approaching two supervisors simultaneously for the same scholarship
Using your prospective UCAS supervisor as a referee, which the call prohibits
Incomplete or non-compliant uploads, which may simply not be processed, and any inaccuracy found later revokes the application or offer
Assuming the partial tier is the default: it carries no stipend and no accommodation
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Board expenses and travel expenses, plus experiment, meeting and training costs beyond the curriculum, are at the student's own expense. Accommodation outside Beijing or beyond the basic allocation is charged to awardees as their host institutes request, and shared rooms run about RMB 30/day with single rooms about RMB 60/day.
document_audit: The CV must cover education from university onwards, and employed applicants need an employment certificate attached
Final degree certificates and transcripts for pre-graduation applicants must be uploaded later through the host college before registration, not sent separately
Published papers should be limited to five, first page and abstract only; unpublished work must not be included
All scanned originals must be colour scans, and any non-English/Chinese document must be merged with its translation into one PDF
The two-inch bareheaded photo must match your passport photo exactly
alerts: The 31 January 2026 deadline was earlier than the 15 April 2026 general admission window, so scholarship applicants must work to the scholarship clock, not the admission clock
Awardees must sit the annual review; failing it suspends or removes the scholarship, so the funding is not guaranteed for the full 36 months
All work published during the funding period must be credited to the host school/CAS institute and UCAS and must acknowledge the UCAS Scholarship
The 2026 round is closed and the deadlined route applies to PhD and Master's applicants only, while visiting-student routes remain open with no deadline
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One submission through is.ucas.ac.cn with the scholarship selected inside the admission application, followed by document review and a mainly interview-based entrance examination run by the chosen college or institute.
